hook.line: Off-camera voice: with zero experience, how would you get a marketing job in 30 days?
hook.visual: Wide shot of a woman typing at a curved wooden desk; the camera pushes in as she turns to the lens under a serif 'How to work in Marketing' title.

beats.what: Wide office shot, she types at the desk while an off-camera voice asks the question
Slow push-in toward her as she looks up from the keyboard
Title clears and single-word yellow captions start at the top of frame
She picks up the mic and starts answering ('That's a tough one')
Core tip: find jobs that excite you and build a mock campaign for each company
Concrete example: a mock Coachella social campaign for a named beauty brand
Payoff: the extra step proves you are creative without direct experience
Abrupt 'Bye' with a wave, no call to action

why_it_works: An off-camera question frames the video as a candid ask, so the viewer hears the problem in their own words
One single tip with a specific named example (mock campaign for a real brand at a real event) is easy to act on
The aspirational office setting and the push-in from typing to speaking make it feel caught mid-work
Short (39.7 s) with one unbroken shot and an abrupt 'Bye', which helps it loop (loop 0.864)
weaknesses: No cuts at all and a small face (median height 0.084), so nothing visual changes for 37 s
Very quiet mix (-33.4 LUFS) compared with typical feeds
No CTA, so viewers who liked it get no next step
for_robert: Open with an off-camera question, which Fred could ask from the corner of the frame, then answer with one concrete example; skip the long static shot.
